text:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache error rate spike detected for cluster us-west-2-gpu-prod. metric: prefix_cache_invalidation_rate jumped to 3200/min at 3029100000. paging oncall.

derek: paging in. seeing 5xx rate up ~12% on inference path, latency tails 99p -> 1.8s. is this the batch-config rollout from 3029096400? @carla any rollout notes?

carla: yep, we shipped batch-config v2.3.1 at ~3029096300. main change: aggressive continuous batching (max_batch_wait_ms=40 -> 120) + optimistic prefix prefetch. rollout to 20% initially.

eva: logs show KV store churn and prefix cache growth. sample log:
```
[3029099850] prefix_cache.size=78k prefix_cache.evictions=12k/sec kv_prefetch_queue=4500
[3029099861] cache_write_latency=250ms rss=21GB
[3029099872] continuous_batch_flushes=high template_hash_mismatch=340
```

frank: template_hash_mismatch - that looks like prompt template drift. I also see tokenization checksum mismatches: tokenizer_v2 vs tokenizer_v2-lite mismatch for a subset of requests coming from routed clients.

oncall-sre: quick triage: impact appears to be amplified when batching window increases because more distinct prompt prefixes are accumulated and the prefetch layer tries to prime kv keys that collide due to an upstream tokenizer change -> cache key explosion. customers affected: high-rate streaming customers and dedicated pools in us-west-2.

derek: mitigation plan proposals: 1) revert batch-config to previous values (v2.3.0) 2) temporarily disable optimistic prefetch 3) apply tokenization compatibility guard (reject mismatched tokenizer versions at router)

carla: working on 1 and 2 in parallel. I can push a hotpatch to dedicated pools only first. command I'm about to run:
```
# rollback batch-config to v2.3.0 for us-west-2-gpu-prod-dedicated
rctl rollout set batch-config v2.3.0 --scope cluster:us-west-2-gpu-prod-dedicated --strategy immediate
# disable optimistic prefetch
rctl set feature prefetch.optimistic=false --scope cluster:us-west-2
```

incident-bot: DEPLOY_STARTED: rctl rollout set batch-config v2.3.0 (id: r-99321) by carla at 3029100090

eva: putting a small traffic-shed on affected pool (rate-limit 20% on streaming route) to reduce burst while rollback proceeds. applying rate-limiting rule now.

ops-lead: good. also add a short-term KV write throttle on prefetch namespace to prevent further growth: `kvctl throttle set prefetch 1000/s` —set to 1000/s for 30m.

frank: on tokenizer incompatibility: I'm preparing a compatibility check at router. quick patch:
```
# router patch (hotfix)
if request.meta.tokenizer != model.tokenizer: reject 409 "tokenizer mismatch" with header X-Token-Compat: need:model.tokenizer
```
We'll return a structured error so SDKs can fallback.
```

derek: prioritize rollback + throttle first. if we get cache size down and 5xxs <1% we can hold. carla, estimate time for rollback to hit 100% of dedicated pool?

carla: immediate strategy means within ~90s for pool nodes to pick new config; full convergence ~6m. optimistic prefetch toggle is instant for new connections.

incident-bot: DEPLOY_SUCCESS: r-99321 completed at 3029100205 (targets: us-west-2-gpu-prod-dedicated) by carla

eva: observing metrics: prefix_cache.size dropping from 78k -> 18k over last 2m. error rate trending down; 99p latency back to 740ms. still seeing a few template_hash_mismatch errors but much reduced.

oncall-sre: good. keep kv throttle for another 15 minutes and then step down. frank, deploy the router compatibility guard as a canary (5%) to verify behavior.

frank: canary deployed to 5% at 3029100255. logs show expected 409 responses for 0.3% of requests; SDKs from one partner handled fallback fine.

customer-success-bot: Notifying CS about visible customer impact: CS ticket created #CS-9273. Customers A and B reported elevated timeouts. message sent to account teams.

derek: handoff notes for postmortem: root cause = combined change: increased batch wait + optimistic prefetch caused more distinct prefixes to be prefetched; upstream tokenizer rollout created inconsistent prompt hashing resulting in cache key explosion and KV write amplification.

carla: immediate followups: (1) add pre-deploy check that model.tokenizer == upstream tokenization_version for routes with prefetch enabled (2) add a guard in prefetch to cap concurrent outstanding prefetches per-prefix (3) create a dashboard showing prefix_cache_unique_keys / prefetch_queue_size.

eva: customer impact summary for the oncall handoff: affected ~4 dedicated pools, ~2.1M requests over 10m window, SLO violations for 18 customers with 3 showing user-facing timeouts. mitigation reduced 5xxs to baseline in ~4m.

ops-lead: leaving a note: we escalated correctly, rollback + throttle + canary router guard worked. We'll schedule postmortem in incidents-review next Tue 3029102000. assign carla (owner), frank (tokenizer action), eva (metrics/dashboard), derek (postmortem write).

incident-bot: THREAD_RESOLVED: service stabilized at 3029100360. auto-close will not occur until postmortem is linked. :white_check_mark:

oncall-sre: final: snapshot configs, logs, and a minimal reproducer in the incident-runbook repo. adding links in the postmortem doc. thanks everyone for fast response. :thumbsup:
